keyVerseText: And Ezekias begat Manasses; and Manasses begat Amon; and Amon begat Josias;
rootMeaning: The Greek name Μανασσῆς (Manassēs) derives from the Hebrew מְנַשֶּׁה (Mᵉnashsheh), which means "causing to forget." This etymology suggests a sense of releasing or letting go of past burdens or hardships. Beyond the common English transliteration 'Manasses,' the root meaning highlights a theological motif of forgetting or releasing, which can be understood as God enabling His people to move beyond previous troubles or sins.
usageInScripture: The word Μανασσῆς appears three times in the New Testament, primarily translated as 'Manasses' twice and once as 'of Manasses.' It designates both a personal name and a tribal identity, referencing the firstborn son of Joseph and the tribe descending from him, as well as a king of Judah. This consistency in usage underscores its role as a proper noun tied to Israelite heritage and lineage, affirming its significance in biblical genealogies and historical records.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Manassēs as 'causing to forget' enriches our grasp of biblical themes such as forgiveness, restoration, and divine grace. The name's connection to both a patriarchal figure and a king reflects God's sovereign work through individuals and tribes in His redemptive plan. For the Christian faith, it reminds believers that God can help us release our past failures and walk forward in newness of life. This aligns with the gospel message that through Christ, our sins are forgotten and we are adopted into God's family, just as Manassēs represents a foundational link in the lineage leading to the Messiah.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 1:10 states, 'And Ezekias begat Manasses; and Manasses begat Amon; and Amon begat Josias,' highlighting Manasses as a crucial link in the genealogy of Jesus. The use of this name here connects the Messiah to the historical and spiritual heritage of Israel. The meaning of Manassēs as 'causing to forget' subtly enriches this genealogy, suggesting that through this lineage, God’s plan includes the forgiveness and renewal of His people, culminating in the coming of Christ.
